skill.name: bolder
skill.description: Amplify safe or boring interface designs with stronger hierarchy, color, typography, composition, and motion while preserving usability.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents to make frontend designs more distinctive, memorable, and usable.
skill.author: pbakaus

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by design vocabulary in SKILL.md. The skill provides frontend design guidance and shows no evidence of reconnaissance, exfiltration, prompt injection, or unsafe tool use.

static_findings.snippet: - **Timid scale**: Everything is medium-sized with no drama
- **Bold palette**: Introduce unexpected color combinations—avoid the purple-blue gradient AI slop
**The test**: If you showed this to someone and said "AI made this bolder," would they believe you i

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 25 uses "Timid scale" to describe visual hierarchy in interface design. It does not request host, OS, or environment reconnaissance.
Line 66 discusses color palette choices for UI design. The phrase has no connection to system inspection or privileged environment discovery.
Line 117 is a quality test for avoiding generic AI-looking design. It does not instruct reconnaissance, collection, or security bypass behavior.
Lines 92-93 introduce a composition design section about hero moments. There is no network access, scanning, endpoint discovery, or external communication.

content.value_statement: Many interfaces feel safe, flat, or generic. Bolder gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured way to add impact while preserving usability.
actual_capabilities: Identifies weak visual hierarchy, low contrast, static layouts, and generic design choices.
Plans a focused boldness direction based on brand, audience, purpose, and constraints.
Recommends stronger typography, color, spacing, composition, visual effects, and motion.
Warns against generic AI design patterns like repeated purple-blue gradients and glassmorphism.
Checks the final design for usability, accessibility, coherence, memorability, and performance.
limitations: It depends on available design context and may ask for clarification before changing a product.
It does not generate production assets by itself unless the host agent has suitable tools.
It focuses on frontend visual direction, not backend behavior or business logic.
It cannot guarantee brand approval when formal brand guidelines are missing.

use_cases.title: Refresh a conservative product page
use_cases.description: Turn a flat marketing page into a more memorable experience without losing clarity or conversion goals.

use_cases.title: Improve a functional dashboard
use_cases.description: Add stronger hierarchy, accent color, and purposeful motion while keeping repeated workflows easy to scan.

use_cases.title: Review AI-generated interface work
use_cases.description: Find generic visual choices and replace them with a coherent direction that feels more intentional.

prompt_templates.title: Make a screen bolder
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bolder on this screen. Keep the current purpose, but improve hierarchy, color, spacing, and visual energy.

prompt_templates.title: Strengthen a product flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bolder on the checkout flow. Add a stronger focal point and clearer hierarchy without reducing trust or readability.

prompt_templates.title: Create a brand-aware boldness plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bolder for this SaaS dashboard. Build a visual strategy that respects our brand, audience, accessibility needs, and performance limits.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and redesign a full interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bolder to audit this interface, identify weak design choices, propose a focused direction, implement improvements, and verify usability.

output_examples.input: A homepage uses centered text, muted colors, and equal spacing everywhere.
output_examples.output: The skill would propose one dominant hero moment, sharper type scale, a richer palette, and controlled asymmetry for more impact.

output_examples.input: A dashboard is useful but visually flat and hard to scan quickly.
output_examples.output: The skill would strengthen key metrics, reduce equal visual weight, add purposeful accents, and preserve dense operational readability.

output_examples.input: An AI-generated landing page relies on glass effects and purple-blue gradients.
output_examples.output: The skill would flag those generic choices and replace them with a more specific visual direction tied to the product.

best_practices: Provide brand, audience, accessibility, and performance constraints before asking for major visual changes.
Choose one primary focal point so the interface feels intentional instead of loud.
Verify readability, task completion, and motion comfort after each boldness pass.
anti_patterns: Do not add effects only because the current design feels quiet.
Do not make every element visually dominant, because hierarchy will collapse.
Do not replace brand strategy with generic gradients, glass panels, or neon accents.

faq.question: What does this skill do?
faq.answer: It helps an AI agent make frontend designs more distinctive while preserving usability and coherence.

faq.question: Is this only for landing pages?
faq.answer: No. It can guide product pages, dashboards, flows, and other interface surfaces.

faq.question: Does it ignore accessibility?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly checks readability, WCAG needs, motion comfort, and functional clarity.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing brand?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the agent to consider brand personality, constraints, audience, and purpose before pushing the design.

faq.question: Does it create code automatically?
faq.answer: The skill gives design direction. Code changes depend on the host agent and the tools available in the workspace.

faq.question: Why does it warn about AI design patterns?
faq.answer: It discourages common generic effects so the final interface feels specific, confident, and product appropriate.
